title: Work Tracking QA
eyebrow: QA, second round · background work tracking (parent issue #396, "every layer of delegated work is one tap away"), house-rules 2.73.2

short.lead: Background work tracking is ready for QA again, on branch AjsAgent/background-work-tracking as house-rules 2.73.2 (pull request #402). The first round failed so that no known gap reaches main, so three more steps were added. The helper ledger, the feature names and the cloud update check are fixed (#403). Nothing the plugin writes credits Claude, and no claude.ai session, project, artifact or share link can reach git (#405). The docs are updated (#404). verify.py passes all 963 checks and verify_tools.py all 47. The four steps from the first round are unchanged, and the test for you is the same one.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what was checked and how.
items: Unchanged since the first round: five verify.py cases pass, and the session-start hook produced this thread's own link from the real environment.
Unchanged since the first round: five verify.py cases pass. It has still not seen a real Remote Control start.
Unchanged since the first round: four verify.py cases pass, and a real helper's transcript rendered to a file listing its 19 shell commands.
Unchanged since the first round: eight verify.py cases pass, and a run over the first thread's real transcript flagged exactly the checklists that lacked the link.
Helper ledger, feature names and the cloud update check (#403)

New verify.py cases pass for all three. I also ran the fixed name cleaner on the names the design loop really stored for this feature: "background work tracking 1A 2A</message>" and "background work tracking 1*" both become "background work tracking", and "3D printer" stays whole. The update check, run against this session's real synced plugin copy, printed one plain line saying the copy is synced from your account and cannot be updated by command here, with no update command.
No Claude credit and no claude.ai links reach git (#405)

The plugin's own safety commit for a helper now ends with "Committed by AJ's agent"; a verify.py case makes a real one and reads its message back. The guard refuses an artifact link in a commit message, a share link in a pull request body, an artifact link on a staged file line (naming the file and line), the same link when a git add in the same command would stage it, and links in files written through the GitHub tools. A commit whose docs only name the claude.ai code address in prose passes. A search of the whole branch for session, project, artifact and share links finds none: the three real artifact links in docs/plans are gone, and every test link is built from two parts.
Try it in a new project thread
After 2.73.2 is installed, start a new thread in a claude.ai project, ask for a task that uses a helper agent, then one that starts a Remote Control session on your PC.
Check that the checklist header links to the thread's transcript, a helper's work-trail file is attached, and "Transcript of the session on your PC" is posted without you asking. Open each one.

unverified: No session has run 2.73.2 yet, because hooks load at session start; every check drove the branch's hook.py directly or called its functions
No real Remote Control session was started, so the rclink hook has only seen recorded results, and whether claude.ai runs hooks for that tool at all waits on your test
The fixed helper ledger was checked by a verify.py case on a fixture transcript, not on a real helper, because no helper ran in this session
A commit through a cd or -C the guard cannot follow skips the new link check; the rest of the guard still asks about that command
GitHub may still add its own footer to a pull request body in a cloud session; the read-back reports it rather than preventing it
